run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T02:56:10Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by an unsuccessful replacement of the single ad service pod. At 02:57:30 the ad Deployment created ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 and its controller stopped the only old pod (ad-554b849958-w5fhc, 'Stopping container ad' 02:57:32). The new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was placed in the ad Service endpoints before its application was listening, because the Deployment defines no readiness or liveness probe, and its container was pinned at its 50m CPU limit with 95-99% of CFS periods throttled. Its earliest retained log line 'Ad service starting.' is 2026-11-15T03:02:19Z. From ~02:57:43 the frontend's gRPC GetAds calls to the ad ClusterIP 100.70.197.56:8080 failed with '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' in sub-100 ms (refused connections, not timeouts), which made frontend's /api/data route return HTTP 500, which frontend-proxy relayed as 500 on both its 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans. frontend-proxy's ingress error ratio rose from ~0.1% to 1.6% at 02:59, peaked at 7.9-8.0% at 03:03-03:05 and was back to 0.1-0.4% by 03:11-03:15 as ad resumed serving. A separate, much smaller error signal (0.03-0.12% frontend-proxy 503s whose egress call to frontend returned status 0, present from ~02:41) predates the burst and is the most likely reason the >0 threshold was crossed already at 02:56:10; its cause is unresolved.

claims.text: At 03:05 the frontend-proxy spans of the last 10 minutes showed errors on its own span names: 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.6737/s against UNSET 11.5035/s, and 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.6544/s against UNSET 11.5211/s. The alerting entity itself therefore records error spans.

The frontend-proxy ingress error ratio (ERROR spans / all 'ingress' spans, 5m rate) was 0 at 02:37:10 and 02:39:10, small but nonzero 0.03-0.12% from 02:41:10 through 02:57:10, then 1.64% at 02:59:10, 4.97% at 03:01:10, 7.94% at 03:03:10, 8.02% at 03:05:10, 6.93% at 03:07:10, 2.36% at 03:09:10, 0.12% at 03:11:10 and 0.44% at 03:15:10.

A sampled error trace (df313cdaac0af99f3c8290c54dfde1a2) shows the exact chain: frontend span 'GET' http.status_code 500 -> 'GET /api/data' 500 -> 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 500 with exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' -> child client span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' with otel.status_code ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code 14. The failing GetAds spans in this sample completed in roughly 0.3-101 ms.

100.70.197.56:8080 is the Service 'ad' ClusterIP and port (clusterIP 100.70.197.56, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad). The refused address in the error text is therefore the ad Service, not an individual pod IP; ad's current endpoint address is 100.96.3.224:8080.

Kubernetes events for the ad workload: ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 'SuccessfulCreate' pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh 02:57:30, pod 'Scheduled' 02:57:30, container 'Created' 02:57:31, 'Started container ad' 02:57:32, and ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 'SuccessfulDelete' of pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc with 'Killing: Stopping container ad' at 02:57:32. ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 (created 02:25:24) now has 0 replicas; ad-785b4464f5 (created 02:57:30) has 1 ready.

The ad Deployment is a single replica (replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1) with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and both readinessProbe and livenessProbe null; its status shows observedGeneration 2 and condition NewReplicaSetAvailable with lastUpdateTime 02:57:32.

The new ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh's earliest retained log line is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-15T03:02:19.907Z, about 4m47s after its container was reported Started at 02:57:32; the 339 following lines run only to 03:08:20 and are normal request lines such as 'Targeted ad request received for [telescopes]' and 'Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.'

The ad service's own server-span rate for 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' (5m rate) fell from 0.796/s at the 02:57 sample and 0.4519/s at 02:59 to 0.0037/s at 03:01 and 0/s at 03:03, then recovered to 0.2449/s at 03:05, 0.5665/s at 03:07 and 0.9240/s at 03:09; ad reported no STATUS_CODE_ERROR for any of its operations in this window.

CPU throttling differs sharply between the two ad pods: the new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh had a throttled-periods ratio of 0.947 at 02:58 rising to 0.97-0.99 through 03:05 (0.65 at 03:09, 0.27-0.30 at 03:11-03:15), while the old pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc ran at 0.088-0.18. The new pod's CPU usage ramped from 0.008 to 0.0986 cores between 02:58 and 03:05 and then declined; the old pod used 0.010-0.016 cores. Both ReplicaSet pod templates declare limits cpu 50m, memory 450Mi.

The two ad ReplicaSet pod templates (ad-554b849958 and ad-785b4464f5) show the same image tag, the same container port 8080, the same env variable names and the same resources; the ad Deployment's observedGeneration moved to 2 and a new ReplicaSet appeared, but the specific spec field changed at ~02:57:30 is not visible in the current objects.
The frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-kxdcl is Running and ready with 0 restarts (started 02:25:29), and the frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw is Running and ready with 0 restarts.

frontend's own error spans in the 10 minutes to 03:05 are confined to the ad path and its /api/data route: 'GET' ERROR 0.6544/s, 'GET /api/data' 0.6544/s, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 0.6544/s and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' ERROR 0.6544/s, while 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'CartService/AddItem', 'CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart' and 'POST /api/checkout' all show STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.

The earliest ECONNREFUSED-to-ad failures I observed in the sampled traces are at 02:57:43.1, 02:57:43.2, 02:57:44.4 and 02:57:44.9 (frontend-proxy ingress 500 / egress 500 / frontend GET 500 / GetAds grpc 14), and the frontend GetAds 1-minute error rate is first nonzero at the 02:59:00 sample (1.63/s), peaking 1.97/s at 03:03:00 and returning to 0 at 03:07:00. Sampled traces are biased; earlier instances may exist unseen.

Before the burst, frontend-proxy already emitted occasional 503s: ingress spans with http.status_code 503 (durations 26.4 ms, 55.8 ms and 615.8 ms) around 02:54:49-02:56:32, whose child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error=true and http.status_code=0. A whole-trace fetch of trace 0a94ed1338bcd020bdd12b107f2521a3 contains only those two proxy spans - no frontend span exists for the failed request.

Service-level STATUS_CODE_ERROR rates over the 10 minutes to 03:05 were returned only for frontend (2.6439/s), frontend-proxy (1.3281/s), recommendation (0.00175/s) and fraud-detection (0.00175/s), with explicit 0 for ad, payment and accounting; no ERROR series was returned for cart, checkout, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, kafka, image-provider or load-generator, which leaves their error state unknown rather than proven zero.

The fraud-detection pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 was OOMKilled (exitCode 137) at 02:32:08 and restarted once; its container has been running and ready since 02:32:08 with restarts 1. Its own error span rate is 0.00175/s, two orders of magnitude below frontend's 2.6439/s.

frontend-proxy ingress p95 latency (histogram_quantile over 5m rate of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket) moved only modestly: 520-567 ms at the 02:37-02:45 baseline, 657 ms at 02:57, 671-727 ms at 02:59-03:03, 687-766 ms at 03:05-03:13 and 814 ms at 03:15.

Primary cause of the alert's large error reading: the ad Service had no listening backend after its single-replica rolling replacement at 02:57:30. Because the ad Deployment defines no readiness probe, the new pod was placed in the Service endpoints before its application listened (earliest log 'Ad service starting.' at 03:02:19), so frontend's gRPC channel to the ad ClusterIP received ECONNREFUSED from ~02:57:43 until ad resumed serving; frontend translated that into HTTP 500 on /api/data, which frontend-proxy reported as its own ingress and egress errors (peak 7.9-8.0% at 03:03-03:05).

Why the new ad pod needed roughly 5 minutes before serving: its container was effectively starved by its 50m CPU limit during startup, shown by 0.947-0.99 throttled-period ratio and usage pinned at ~0.0986 cores from 02:58 to 03:05, versus 0.09-0.18 throttling and 0.010-0.016 cores on the old pod. The correlation with the delayed 'Ad service starting.' line at 03:02:19 supports CPU starvation as the mechanism, but the startup profile itself was not measured directly.

Why the alert is dated 02:56:10, before the ad burst: the pre-existing low-level 503 signal (frontend-proxy ingress 503 whose egress call to frontend returned status 0, ratio 0.03-0.12% from 02:41:10 onward) is the most plausible trigger for a threshold of 'error rate above 0'. This candidate remains open; its upstream-failure mechanism is not established by the evidence.

The ad application itself did not report failures: none of ad's span series carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the window, its GetAds server spans are STATUS_CODE_UNSET throughout, and the 340 retained ad log lines (03:02:19-03:08:20) are ordinary request-handling lines. The observed breakage is a connection-level refusal at the Service VIP, not ad returning error responses.

frontend-proxy kept serving normal traffic throughout: its ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate stayed around 11.5/s with only 0.67/s errors at 03:05, its pod was ready with 0 restarts, and its p95 latency stayed in the 657-814 ms band against a 520-567 ms baseline, so the alert is not the result of the proxy itself failing or of a large latency excursion.

Slow ad responses / deadline exceeded: rejected. The failing GetAds client spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with the explicit text 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' and completed in roughly 0.3-101 ms, which is a refused connection, not a timeout.

ad pod crash, OOM or restart loop as the reason ad stopped serving: rejected for the observed period. Pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh shows restarts 0, an empty lastState and a running container since 02:57:32, and ad-554b849958-w5fhc was removed by its own controller's rolling replacement ('SuccessfulDelete' plus new-pod 'Started') rather than by eviction; no OOMKilled or Evicted mark was seen on either ad pod.

fraud-detection's OOMKill at 02:32 as the cause of this alert: rejected for this cause. It is a different service, its own error rate is 0.00175/s versus frontend's 2.6439/s and frontend-proxy's error path is the ad/GetAds chain, its restart happened about 25 minutes before the alert and no evidence links it to the frontend-proxy errors. Its OOMKill remains a fact about that pod, unattributed to this incident.

Other frontend backends (cart, checkout, product-catalog) failing into the same 500 path: rejected. frontend's client spans for CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder have STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0 in the incident window, and their UNSET call rates continue normally (for example GetCart 2.96/s), so only the AdService branch is failing.

Add a readiness probe (gRPC/HTTP health check on port 8080) and ideally a startupProbe to the ad Deployment so a replacement pod is not added to the ad Service endpoints before it is listening; this alone would have converted the outage into a zero-error rollout.

Raise the ad container CPU limit above 50m (or remove the limit while keeping the request) so startup is not throttled to roughly 5 minutes, and re-check throttling after the change; also review whether a single replica without a PodDisruptionBudget/maxUnavailable guard is acceptable for ad.

Investigate the intermittent frontend-proxy 503s independently of the ad incident: they appear as ingress 503 with a 'router frontend egress' span in error state with http.status_code 0 and no corresponding frontend span, and they started around 02:41, so they need their own root cause rather than being attributed to the ad rollout.

gaps: The ad Deployment spec change that triggered the 02:57:30 rollout (observedGeneration 2, new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5) is not visible: change_history is not an integrated source in this run, and the two ReplicaSet pod templates match on image, port, env names and resources.

The alert rule 'RequestErrorRate' is not available in the queried Prometheus: the rule lookup by rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data (79832247-5344-4cc5-b1f1-30aa19338dfa-t1:4782c840-df8c-4e20-87c5-d1a5dfb26471), so its expression, threshold and 'for' duration are unknown; the annotated value 2.4555 cannot be reproduced exactly from the available series and the reason the alert is dated 02:56:10 (before the ad burst) is inferred only.

kube-state-metrics series were not returned: kube_pod_info for ad pods (af67ed67-75bb-4575-8407-6d41c198e1ca-t1:456819f6-9196-4f8c-90dd-364140d8b6b3) and the kube_* name listing (bc513b1a-5362-4e14-ba55-dd5167c3067b-t0:54b9b3f6-6ed8-4966-85dc-623dd85ffd14), http_* name listing (bc513b1a-5362-4e14-ba55-dd5167c3067b-t1:0d370187-04bc-4f8d-82dd-23701b411e51), the explicit kube_endpoint/kube_pod_status_ready/http_server metric-name query (11d61a62-445b-462f-9c23-0d62c12e16b8-t0:2992861c-cf76-49ab-a6d3-97cc09e369d3) and the rpc_*/http_server metric-name query (89ae7950-deaa-4307-aa4e-93d42869b3ab-t1:d818b888-9904-4369-b43f-dcd1dbd06853) all returned no_data; endpoint readiness and deployment replica counts therefore cannot be charted over time, and endpoint state is known only from objects read after the fact.
The old ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc no longer exists, so its logs, IP and whether it was already degraded before 02:57:32 cannot be checked.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines: the log query on frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw returned no_data (e1f8ee57-0e4b-4822-be4f-a232d830f7ee-t1:41acd253-656c-4660-a173-8ff908928f99), so frontend-side application logs could not corroborate the 500s.

The log window between the new pod's Start (02:57:32) and its first retained line (03:02:19) is not covered: the log query for 02:57:28-02:59:00 returned no_data (9b942f4c-20e9-4218-8cd3-971b0291d7fb-t0:ddb4dcd7-a10e-4b40-a0b9-04d7839fa92c), and the error-filtered ad log query also returned no_data (b1f77867-5962-4a76-b54b-b04b25f0784c-t1:9920c50d-5a59-47c7-8f03-0fad70848892), which is not evidence of absence; whether the app failed or merely started slowly between 02:57:32 and 03:02:19 cannot be distinguished.

The cause of the intermittent frontend-proxy 503 / egress status 0 failures from ~02:41 is unresolved; no frontend span exists for the failed requests in the trace examined, and the sampled trace list for the ad-afflicted path was returned incomplete (17ba8303-114a-4303-8b40-55afce989b60-t0:a7af8f33-055b-494b-9b04-d4c9176954c0) so more error traces may exist than were shown.
Node-level CPU/memory pressure was not examined, so whether host contention contributed to the new ad pod's throttling is unknown.

No ERROR series was returned for cart, checkout, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, kafka, image-provider or load-generator, so their error state in this window is unknown rather than verified zero.
next_steps: Inspect the ad Deployment's rollout history/change record (not available here) to learn what changed at 02:57:30 and why the replacement pod was created.
Add and validate a readiness probe plus a startupProbe on the ad Deployment, and raise its 50m CPU limit; then re-run a single-replica rollout during low traffic to confirm no error-rate increase.
Fetch the actual RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression, window, 'for') from the alerting stack to reconcile the 02:56:10 start and the 2.4555 value with the observed 0.03-8.0% range.
Collect endpoint readiness (kube-state-metrics kube_endpoint_address or kube_pod_status_ready) so Service-without-endpoints periods are directly observable.
Open a separate investigation into the intermittent frontend-proxy 503 with upstream 'router frontend egress' status 0 starting around 02:41.

Because the ad Deployment defines no readiness probe, the new pod was placed in the Service endpoints before its application listened (earliest log 'Ad service starting.' at 03:02:19), so frontend's gRPC channel to the ad ClusterIP received ECONNREFUSED from ~02:57:43 until ad resumed serving; frontend translated that into HTTP 500 on /api/data, which frontend-proxy reported as its own ingress and egress errors (peak 7.9-8.0% at 03:03-03:05).

Why the new ad pod needed roughly 5 minutes before serving: its container was effectively starved by its 50m CPU limit during startup, shown by 0.947-0.99 throttled-period ratio and usage pinned at ~0.0986 cores from 02:58 to 03:05, versus 0.09-0.18 throttling and 0.010-0.016 cores on the old pod. The correlation with the delayed 'Ad service starting.' line at 03:02:19 supports CPU starvation as the mechanism, but the startup profile itself was not measured directly.

Why the alert is dated 02:56:10, before the ad burst: the pre-existing low-level 503 signal (frontend-proxy ingress 503 whose egress call to frontend returned status 0, ratio 0.03-0.12% from 02:41:10 onward) is the most plausible trigger for a threshold of 'error rate above 0'. This candidate remains open; its upstream-failure mechanism is not established by the evidence.

recommendation.text: Add a readiness probe (gRPC/HTTP health check on port 8080) and ideally a startupProbe to the ad Deployment so a replacement pod is not added to the ad Service endpoints before it is listening; this alone would have converted the outage into a zero-error rollout.

Raise the ad container CPU limit above 50m (or remove the limit while keeping the request) so startup is not throttled to roughly 5 minutes, and re-check throttling after the change; also review whether a single replica without a PodDisruptionBudget/maxUnavailable guard is acceptable for ad.

Investigate the intermittent frontend-proxy 503s independently of the ad incident: they appear as ingress 503 with a 'router frontend egress' span in error state with http.status_code 0 and no corresponding frontend span, and they started around 02:41, so they need their own root cause rather than being attributed to the ad rollout.

counter_evidence.text: The ad application itself did not report failures: none of ad's span series carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the window, its GetAds server spans are STATUS_CODE_UNSET throughout, and the 340 retained ad log lines (03:02:19-03:08:20) are ordinary request-handling lines. The observed breakage is a connection-level refusal at the Service VIP, not ad returning error responses.

frontend-proxy kept serving normal traffic throughout: its ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate stayed around 11.5/s with only 0.67/s errors at 03:05, its pod was ready with 0 restarts, and its p95 latency stayed in the 657-814 ms band against a 520-567 ms baseline, so the alert is not the result of the proxy itself failing or of a large latency excursion.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Slow ad responses / deadline exceeded: rejected. The failing GetAds client spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code 14 with the explicit text 'No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' and completed in roughly 0.3-101 ms, which is a refused connection, not a timeout.

ad pod crash, OOM or restart loop as the reason ad stopped serving: rejected for the observed period. Pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh shows restarts 0, an empty lastState and a running container since 02:57:32, and ad-554b849958-w5fhc was removed by its own controller's rolling replacement ('SuccessfulDelete' plus new-pod 'Started') rather than by eviction; no OOMKilled or Evicted mark was seen on either ad pod.

fraud-detection's OOMKill at 02:32 as the cause of this alert: rejected for this cause. It is a different service, its own error rate is 0.00175/s versus frontend's 2.6439/s and frontend-proxy's error path is the ad/GetAds chain, its restart happened about 25 minutes before the alert and no evidence links it to the frontend-proxy errors. Its OOMKill remains a fact about that pod, unattributed to this incident.

Other frontend backends (cart, checkout, product-catalog) failing into the same 500 path: rejected. frontend's client spans for CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder have STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0 in the incident window, and their UNSET call rates continue normally (for example GetCart 2.96/s), so only the AdService branch is failing.
